source.title: From Local to Global to Mechanistic: An iERF-Centered Unified Framework for Interpreting Vision Models
source.authors: Yearim Kim; Sang-Yu Han; N. Kwak

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no relevant cut-off or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses SAEs to extract vision-model concepts and reports their reconstruction quality, but it does not test whether SAE residuals are linearly predictable, scale across SAE sizes, affect model computation, or have distinct linear and nonlinear components.
record.gate_note: Table III reports relative reconstruction error and l0 ratio for SAE, dictionary learning, and bisecting k-means across layers. These results compare concept extractors, not the structure or consequences of SAE residuals. The qualitative SAE-versus-k-means exemplar comparison in Fig. 15 concerns concept coherence, not residual structure.
record.test_reason: The paper uses SAEs (Matryoshka SAE on CLIP ViT-L/14; SAE as one of three concept extractors on ResNet50) as tools. Table III reports relative reconstruction error of SAE vs dictionary learning vs bisecting k-means to choose a node extractor. It does not analyse the structure of SAE error (linear predictability, scaling across sizes, loss effect vs random error, linear/nonlinear split), nor whether keeping the error term matters for circuit analyses. The ICAT graph uses k-means/Lasso reconstructions, not SAE error terms.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct for the Table III portion: bisecting k-means gives the lowest reconstruction error across most layers with competitive sparsity and is adopted as the default node extractor. The paper's main conclusions concern SRD saliency fidelity and robustness, CAFE grounding of non-localized SAE features via iERFs (non-locality rare early, common in deep ViT layers), and ICAT concept graphs with Integrated Gradients as most faithful.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains and compares concept extractors for vision PFVs rather than measuring the original dark-matter residual claims. The SAE setup described for CAFE uses a Matryoshka SAE; Table III reports extractor reconstruction comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported reconstruction metrics vary by layer and concept extractor. Dictionary learning was omitted for Layers 4.0 and 4.2 due to computational cost.

fits_no_version.finding: On ResNet50 PFVs at matched 8x overcompleteness, the SAE (using encoder coefficients) has relative l2 error 1.25-1.90 in layers 1-3, higher than bisecting k-means (0.37-0.69) and dictionary learning (0.60-0.82). In Layers 4.0 and 4.2 it is about 0.48-0.51, comparable to or below k-means.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this CNN PFV concept-extraction setup, SAE reconstruction quality depends strongly on layer and is often worse than clustering-based extractors.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The reconstruction comparison does not characterize error directions, predictability from inputs, tokenwise error norms, error effects on model loss, or scaling with SAE size. Table III reports no uncertainty; dictionary-learning results are absent for Layers 4.0 and 4.2 because of computational cost.
record.rows_left_out: None of the separately reported Table III extractor-by-layer results were left out. No rows were created for qualitative Fig. 15, which compares exemplar coherence rather than SAE reconstruction residuals.

untested.parts: No regression of SAE error on input activations.
No SAE size sweep, per-token error norms or context overlap across sizes.
No spliced-in loss comparison against random errors of equal norm.
No decomposition of error into linear and nonlinear parts.
Circuits are built on k-means concepts; no test of dropping vs keeping an SAE error term.
No comparison of SAE architectures or training objectives with respect to dark matter; the extractor comparison only shows a non-SAE method reconstructs better in this setup.

record.verdict_notes: Rel-l2 values above 1 for the SAE suggest a setup quirk (encoder coefficients possibly not paired with the trained decoder). No uncertainty is reported. Because none of these rows addresses the dark-matter versions, no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test whether SAE error vectors are linearly predictable from input activations.
It does not sweep SAE sizes, measure per-token error norms, compare which contexts larger and smaller SAEs fail on, or test whether error vanishes with scale.
It does not compare model loss after SAE reconstruction replacement with loss after random errors of the same size.
It does not distinguish linear and nonlinear residual components or test whether either component reflects unlearned features or resists dictionary learning.
It does not test whether SAE-based circuit or steering analyses lose model behavior when the error term is omitted.
The extractor comparison is not a test of whether dark matter is mainly an SAE-training artifact, nor does it evaluate improved SAE architectures or end-to-end training.
